6,276 things you can cross, split, or check for real

Everything here is two of something: two columns crossed in one table, a count turned into count-and-share, or — for a proven-real 206 — two tables actually joined. Across 626 datasets. The real joins have not been run yet. 206 pairs are queued and priced, waiting on a go-ahead before touching the warehouse — ask if you want the status.

What counts as moderate

  • Cross-tabs stay inside one table. Kind by place, place by year, kind by kind — no join, just two of the same table's own columns at once instead of one.
  • A share is one division past a count. The number and the percent of the total sit side by side, so a “top” result can't be mistaken for a big one just because it's first.
  • A real join only runs when the key is already proven live in both tables — the same identifiers layer 1 already checked, not a guess at a match.
  • Cross-tabs and shares still haven't been run — same as layer 1, copy the SQL and run it yourself, or ask.
  • Three or more tables, entity resolution, and the full connection map are the next tier up — not here on purpose.
